paragraphs.en: Coding agents are tasked with producing sophisticated interactive applications such as websites, desktop applications, and games. While humans assess these applications interactively, current automated LLM evaluations primarily focus on code analysis and unit tests. This mismatch can cause LLM judges to miss failures that are immediately apparent to human users. We study Interaction-as-a-Judge, an evaluation paradigm where computer-use agents (CUAs) directly interact with an application. We demonstrate that Interaction-as-a-Judge can improve both evaluation and generation of interactive applications. To this end, we collect and release two complementary datasets: 6,858 6,858 pairs of applications with human preferences and corresponding agent traces, and 222 222 applications with human-verified requirement labels. Relative to standard non-interactive approaches, we find that Interaction-as-a-Judge improves evaluation in terms of predicting human preferences ( 65.6 % → 69.1 % 65.6\%\to 69.1\% ) and requirement verification ( 77.0 % → 81.6 % 77.0\%\to 81.6\% ). We also observe scaling benefits: across both preference alignment and requirement verification, higher-quality interactions improve performance. Finally, through both inference- and training-time experiments, we demonstrate that Interaction-as-a-Judge can also improve the quality of generated artifacts. At inference time, Interaction-as-a-Judge repairs 75.5 % 75.5\% of broken requirements within five attempts, compared to 55.4 % 55.4\% for code-only self-feedback. At training time, using Interaction-as-a-Judge as a reward signal improves win-rate over the base model by 6.7 6.7 pp while reducing both generated code length by 35.7 % 35.7\% and build failure rates by 7.2 7.2 pp compared to a code-only reward signal.

paragraphs.en: As coding agents improve, so does the complexity of the software artifacts they produce and, in turn, the difficulty of evaluating those artifacts. Correctness and preference are often difficult to assess from code alone. For example, a game may compile while still failing behaviorally: player animations may not match movement, scene transitions may freeze the application, or interactions may lack the visual and temporal feedback needed to feel responsive and intentional. A natural method for evaluation—and the way most humans evaluate software—is simply to interact with and visually inspect the final product. Yet most current LLM-as-a-Judge ( Zheng et al., 2023 ; Chiang et al., 2024 ) and Agent-as-a-Judge ( Zhuge et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2025 ) methods still rely on static or unimodal inspection of software artifacts. Properly evaluating such artifacts requires moving beyond static inspection to active interaction.
paragraphs.zh: 随着编码智能体的进步，它们所生成的软件产物也日益复杂，而评估这些产物的难度也随之增加。 仅凭代码本身，往往难以判断其正确性并评估其优劣。 例如，一款游戏可能成功编译，但在行为上仍存在缺陷：玩家动画可能与动作不匹配，场景切换可能导致应用冻结，或者交互缺乏必要的视觉和时序反馈，使其无法带来响应迅速且富有意图的体验。 一种自然的评估方法——也是大多数人评估软件的方式——就是直接与最终产品互动并进行视觉检查。 然而，目前大多数“大语言模型作为评判者”（Zheng 等，2023；Chiang 等，2024）和“智能体作为评判者”（Zhuge 等，2024；Li 等，2025）的方法，仍然依赖对软件产物的静态或单模态检查。 要正确评估这类产物，必须超越静态检查，转向主动互动。

paragraphs.en: In this work, we study the use of interaction traces to improve evaluation accuracy and in turn improve generation quality. Concretely, a computer-use agent (CUA) interacts with an application and produces a multimodal interaction trace which can be used to evaluate the quality of the application, or optionally, provide feedback for improving it. We call this evaluation paradigm “Interaction-as-a-Judge” , by analogy with LLM-as-a-Judge ( Zheng et al., 2023 ) . While some prior work has explored this paradigm in different application settings ( Bian et al., 2025 ; Lu et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026 ) , we are the first to systematically study it in a controlled fashion. Specifically, we investigate how dimensions such as interaction strategy and agent capability affect evaluation accuracy for both pairwise human preference prediction and correctness verification. We further show that these evaluation signals can improve generation using simple and standard methods at both inference and training time, namely inference-time scaling and reinforcement learning with a learned reward model.
paragraphs.zh: 在这项工作中，我们研究了如何利用交互痕迹来提高评估准确性，并进而提升生成质量。 具体来说，一个计算机使用智能体（CUA）会与应用程序进行交互，并产生一种多模态交互痕迹，该痕迹可用于评估应用程序的质量，或可选地提供反馈以改进其性能。 我们将这种评估范式称为“交互即裁判”（Interaction-as-a-Judge），以此类推于“大语言模型即裁判”（LLM-as-a-Judge）（Zheng et al., 2023）。 尽管一些先前的研究已在不同的应用场景中探索了这一范式（Bian et al., 2025；Lu et al., 2025；Wang et al., 2026），但我们是首次以受控的方式对其进行系统性研究。 具体而言，我们研究了交互策略和智能体能力等维度如何影响成对的人类偏好预测和正确性验证的评估准确性。 我们还进一步表明，这些评估信号可以通过简单且标准的方法在推理和训练阶段提升生成效果，即推理时的扩展方法以及基于学习奖励模型的强化学习。

paragraphs.en: To study Interaction-as-a-Judge, we introduce two datasets: ArenaPreferences and ArenaCorrectness. ArenaPreferences is a set of 6,858 6,858 agentic code traces across seven different categories of web development (games, simulations, reference-based designs, content-creation tools, brand sites, consumer apps, and data applications). Alongside the agent traces, each data point contains a prompt, two websites generated from the prompt, and labeled human preferences. ArenaCorrectness is a set of 67 67 high-quality game development traces with 828 828 conversation turns. We hand-label 412 412 requirements across various versions of each game as the game develops by interpreting requirements from a user’s prompt and feedback. Requirements are then hand-verified as working or broken depending on if the requirement is successfully implemented.
paragraphs.zh: 为了研究“交互即评判”模式，我们引入了两个数据集：ArenaPreferences 和 ArenaCorrectness。 ArenaPreferences 包含 6,858 条智能体代码追踪记录，涵盖七个不同的网页开发类别（游戏、模拟程序、参考式设计、内容创作工具、品牌网站、消费者应用和数据应用）。 除了智能体追踪记录外，每个数据点还包含一个提示词、两个根据该提示词生成的网站，以及经过标注的人类偏好。 ArenaCorrectness 是一个包含 67 条高质量游戏开发追踪记录和 828 轮对话的高质量数据集。 我们通过解读用户提示词和反馈中的需求，在游戏开发过程中手动标注了各版本游戏的 412 项需求。 随后，根据需求是否成功实现，我们手动验证这些需求是“可用”还是“失效”。

paragraphs.en: We find that Interaction-as-a-Judge increases alignment with human preferences for both in-context LLM judges and trained reward models. On ArenaPreferences, adding interaction traces on top of code significantly improves overall in-context LLM judge accuracy by up to 3.5 3.5 percentage points ( 65.6 % 65.6\% to 69.1 % 69.1\% ) and by 1.5 1.5 percentage points ( 67.6 % 67.6\% to 69.1 % 69.1\% ) when compared to adding only static visual information. Fine-tuning a reward model with interaction traces improves accuracy from 68.2 % 68.2\% to 70.2 % 70.2\% and outperforms in-context LLM judges. We find that higher quality computer-use results in the best overall performance, although even a random heuristic can capture non-trivial gains. On ArenaCorrectness, Interaction-as-a-Judge improves requirement verification accuracy from 77.0 % 77.0\% for a code-only Agent-as-a-Judge ( Zhuge et al., 2024 ) to 81.6 % 81.6\% . At inference-time, we use Interaction-as-a-Judge in a self-feedback loop where an agent iteratively attempts to repair broken requirements and evaluates its repairs using Interaction-as-a-Judge. Compared with code-only feedback, adding interaction to the feedback mechanism increases the percentage of initially broken requirements successfully repaired within five attempts from 55.4 % 55.4\% to 75.5 % 75.5\% . Additionally, we show that websites generated by this post-training recipe attain a 6.7 6.7 pp higher win rate against the base model.

paragraphs.en: In summary, our contributions are as follows:

paragraphs.en: We study Interaction-as-a-Judge for both preference judgements and correctness verification and release two datasets—ArenaPreferences and ArenaCorrectness—for further research into both Interaction-as-a-Judge and agentic generation of interactive applications more broadly.
paragraphs.zh: 我们研究了“交互即判断”方法在偏好判断和正确性验证中的应用，并发布了两个数据集——ArenaPreferences 和 ArenaCorrectness，以支持对“交互即判断”方法以及更广泛的交互式应用智能体生成技术的进一步研究。

paragraphs.en: We show that Interaction-as-a-Judge improves evaluation capabilities. Interaction-as-a-Judge improves overall alignment with human preferences for both in-context LLM judges and trained reward models. Additionally, Interaction-as-a-Judge improves an agent’s ability to verify requirements when compared to a code-only agentic judge.

paragraphs.en: We study Interaction-as-a-Judge under two complementary settings: human preferences and correctness verification. Human preferences are useful when quality is subjective or difficult to capture with explicit requirements, while correctness verification is appropriate when desired behavior can be specified objectively. In many applications, both are necessary. For example, a software application may satisfy its functional requirements while still differing substantially in usability or visual quality. The inverse can also be true, where an application is visually preferable, but functionally broken. Effective evaluation methods should therefore be able to assess both correctness and preference.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在两种互补的设置下研究“交互即评判”方法：人类偏好和正确性验证。 当质量具有主观性或难以通过明确需求进行描述时，人类偏好会很有用；而当期望的行为能够被客观地定义时，正确性验证则更为适用。 在许多应用中，两者都是必要的。 例如，一个软件应用可能满足其功能需求，但在易用性或视觉质量方面仍存在显著差异。 反之亦然：某个应用可能在视觉上更令人满意，但功能上却存在缺陷。 因此，有效的评估方法应当能够同时评估正确性和偏好。

paragraphs.en: We release ArenaPreferences, a dataset of 6,858 6,858 pairwise comparisons across seven categories of web development. We collect our dataset from Arena’s Code Arena where real users prompt two hidden models and vote for their preferred website. Each datapoint in ArenaPreferences contains the user’s prompt, both agentic traces, both final websites, and the ground truth user label. We categorize websites into games, simulations, reference-based designs, content-creation tools, brand sites, consumer product, and data applications following the original leaderboard categories. To ensure that the dataset is high quality, we filter such that all ties are removed, websites are built with React, outputs build successfully, outputs contain ≥ 5 % \geq 5\% character difference, and users spent at least 60 seconds and up to 10 minutes interacting with the websites. All personally identifiable information (PII) has been de-identified through a PII filtering process. To our understanding, this is the largest collection of pairwise agentic web development traces and websites released for open source use. We provide further dataset details in Appendix B .

paragraphs.en: We consider two types of correctness verification: requirement verification and requirement discovery . In requirement verification, the judge is given an application, its code, and a set of explicit requirements, such as “Mario must defeat a Goomba when jumping on it. ” The judge must determine whether each requirement is working or broken for that application. In requirement discovery, the judge is given the application and its code but no explicit list of requirements. It must first identify the relevant requirements automatically and then determine whether those requirements are working.
paragraphs.zh: 我们考虑两种正确性验证类型：需求验证和需求发现。 在需求验证中，评审者会获得一个应用程序、其代码以及一组明确的需求，例如“马里奥在跳上龟壳怪时必须击败它。”评审者必须判断每个需求在该应用程序中是有效还是失效的。 在需求发现中，评审者会获得应用程序及其代码，但没有明确的需求列表。 评审者必须首先自动识别相关需求，然后判断这些需求是否有效。

paragraphs.en: To generate requirements from user traces, we analyze the user trace for specific complaints, and extract the complaint into a broken requirement which is linked to a specific version of the game matching when the user complaint occurred. For example, a user complaint indicating that the player falls through platforms would be annotated as a requirement indicating that the player must be able to stand on platforms. We use GPT 5.6 Luna to label, analyze, and then annotate each complaint as a requirement. A human annotator then reviews each game to verify that the requirements are sensible and broken in the game version. To extract working requirement labels, we take our existing broken requirements, and check to see if the user either explicitly confirms a fix or does not revisit this complaint. We use GPT 5.6 Luna for initial annotation and verify via human annotation. In total, we annotate 323 broken and 89 working requirements. We provide further dataset details in Appendix B .
paragraphs.zh: 为了从用户轨迹中生成需求，我们会分析用户轨迹以查找具体的投诉，并将这些投诉提取为“已失效的需求”，同时将其与用户提出投诉时游戏的具体版本关联起来。 例如，如果用户投诉称玩家会穿过平台，我们就会将其标注为一条需求，即玩家必须能够站在平台上。 我们使用 GPT 5.6 Luna 对每一起投诉进行标记、分析，并将其标注为一条需求。 随后，由人工标注员检查每款游戏，以验证这些需求是否合理，并且是否在该游戏版本中确实失效。 为了提取“有效需求”的标签，我们会基于现有的“已失效需求”，检查用户是否明确确认问题已解决，或者是否不再提及该投诉。 我们使用 GPT 5.6 Luna 进行初步标注，并通过人工标注进行验证。 总共，我们标注了 323 条“已失效需求”和 89 条“有效需求”。 我们在附录 B 中提供了数据集的更多详细信息。

paragraphs.en: Interaction-as-a-Judge is an evaluation paradigm which uses computer-use interaction traces to improve downstream evaluation accuracy. Interaction-as-a-Judge consists of an interaction component and a judge component. These two components can be either the same LLM, different LLMs, or a mixture of LLMs and other methods. For example, a cheap computer-use heuristic paired with an LLM judge, or an LLM-based CUA paired with a trained reward model.

paragraphs.en: Following Koh et al. (2024) , we model interaction with the environment as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP). We define the environment as ℰ = ( 𝒮 , 𝒜 , Ω , f ) \mathcal{E}=(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},\Omega,f) where 𝒮 \mathcal{S} is the state space, 𝒜 \mathcal{A} is the action space, and Ω \Omega is the observation space. In our work, o t ∈ Ω o_{t}\in\Omega is a visual representation of the application (a screenshot), but the Document Object Model (DOM) is also commonly used. An action a t ∈ 𝒜 a_{t}\in\mathcal{A} induces a deterministic transition f : 𝒮 × 𝒜 → 𝒮 f:\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathcal{S} . To interact with the environment, we define an interaction policy π \pi that determines the sequence of actions taken in the environment. Executing π \pi in the environment produces an interaction trace τ = ( ( , , , , , ) ) t = 0 T \tau=((o_{t},\rho_{t},a_{t}))_{t=0}^{T} , where o t o_{t} , ρ t \rho_{t} , and a t a_{t} denote the observation, agent reasoning, and action at timestep t t , respectively. We allow ρ t = ∅ \rho_{t}=\varnothing when no explicit reasoning is produced. Actions include standard computer inputs such as moving the mouse, clicking, and typing—the full action space is in Appendix A.2 .

paragraphs.en: There are multiple approaches to interact with a software application environment, with the primary trade-off being between adaptivity and inference cost. We consider three interaction strategies that vary in how frequently they query a model and observe the resulting environment state.
paragraphs.zh: 与软件应用环境进行交互有多种方法，其主要权衡在于适应性与推理成本之间。 我们考虑了三种交互策略，它们在查询模型以及观察由此产生的环境状态的频率上有所不同。

sents.en: We consider three interaction strategies that vary in how frequently they query a model and observe the resulting environment state.

paragraphs.en: The most general approach is to use a computer-use agent that iteratively observes and acts in the environment. We represent the agent as a policy π θ iter \pi_{\theta}^{\mathrm{iter}} , where at timestep t t it selects an action ( a t , ρ t ) ∼ π θ iter ​ ( τ < t , i ) (a_{t},\rho_{t})\sim\pi_{\theta}^{\mathrm{iter}}(\tau_{<t},i) , where τ < t \tau_{<t} is the interaction trace prior to timestep t t , ρ t \rho_{t} is the reasoning for action a t a_{t} , and i i are instructions to the computer-use agent. For preferences this might be a broad instruction to investigate the application to determine quality while for correctness the goal could be a specific requirement it must verify. The environment then transitions to s t + 1 = f ⁡ ( s t , a t ) s_{t+1}=f(s_{t},a_{t}) , producing a new observation that can inform the next action. This iterative formulation allows the agent to adapt as the environment changes and corresponds to the standard computer-use setting. However, it can be prohibitively expensive, as it requires a model query at every interaction step.

paragraphs.en: A sufficiently capable agent could in principle predict the sequence of actions to take from only the initial state without observing the intermediate outcomes of its actions. paragraphs.en: The cheapest alternative is to forgo model-based action selection entirely. In this work, we consider a simple heuristic policy π heur \pi^{\mathrm{heur}} that selects an action uniformly at random. To make this interaction more effective, we restrict the policy to a candidate set 𝒞 ⁡ ( o t ) ⊆ 𝒜 \mathcal{C}(o_{t})\subseteq\mathcal{A} of interactions that are likely to induce meaningful changes in the environment, such as clicking buttons or typing in text boxes, giving a t ∼ π heur ​ ( o t ) = Unif ⁡ ( 𝒞 ⁡ ( o t ) ) a_{t}\sim\pi^{\mathrm{heur}}(o_{t})=\mathrm{Unif}(\mathcal{C}(o_{t})) . Because this incurs no model inference cost, the policy can select an action after every environment transition. Despite its simplicity, this can produce substantial interaction when 𝒞 ⁡ ( o t ) \mathcal{C}(o_{t}) can be effectively identified, but is less effective for environments such as games, where meaningful interactions are difficult to enumerate automatically.

paragraphs.en: After the interaction trace τ \tau is generated, the judge uses the trace to inform its downstream judgement. We study both an off-the-shelf LLM, which we use for both predicting human preferences and verifying correctness, and a trained reward model, which we use for predicting human preferences. A key benefit of using off-the-shelf LLMs is that it allows interaction-as-a-judge to leverage frontier capabilities without needing to train a custom model, which is often infeasible without data and compute resources. However, a reward model trained on sufficient in-domain data can achieve higher accuracy and reduce inference costs.
paragraphs.zh: 在交互轨迹 τ \tau 生成之后，评判者会利用该轨迹来指导其下游的评判过程。 我们研究了两种模型：一种是我们用于预测人类偏好和验证正确性的现成大型语言模型（LLM），另一种是我们用于预测人类偏好的训练好的奖励模型。 使用现成大型语言模型的一个关键优势在于，它使得“交互即评判”的方法能够利用前沿技术能力，而无需训练一个定制模型——在缺乏数据和计算资源的情况下，后者通常并不可行。 然而，在足够多的领域内数据上训练的奖励模型，可以实现更高的准确性，并降低推理成本。

paragraphs.en: For human preferences, an off-the-shelf LLM judge takes in the user request, source code for each website, and an interaction trace for each website and outputs a judgement indicating which website is better. Due to known position bias ( Zheng et al., 2023 ) , every battle is judged twice with sides swapped (AB and BA) and accuracy is the mean judge-human agreement of both passes. For requirement verification, the judge takes in the user request, the source code, the interaction trace, and a requirements list and labels each requirement as working, broken, or unverifiable. Requirement discovery is similar except no requirement list is given and the judge must output a list of potential requirements itself. For judges that accept video natively, we convert o 0 : T ∈ τ o_{0:T}\in\tau to video; otherwise, we pass in each frame as an image. Actions and reasoning are passed in directly as text sequences.
paragraphs.zh: 对于人类偏好，一个现成的 LLM 裁判会接收用户请求、每个网站的源代码以及每个网站的交互轨迹，并输出一个判断，指出哪个网站更好。 由于已知的位置偏差（Zheng 等人，2023），每场对决都会被两次评判，且每次交换双方角色（AB 和 BA），准确率则是两次评判中与人类一致的平均值。 对于需求验证，裁判会接收用户请求、源代码、交互轨迹和需求列表，并将每个需求标记为“可用”“故障”或“无法验证”。 需求发现与此类似，但不会提供需求列表，裁判必须自行输出一个潜在需求的列表。 对于原生支持视频的裁判，我们将 o 0 : T ∈ τ o_{0:T}\in\tau 转换为视频；否则，我们会将每一帧作为图像传入。 动作和推理会直接以文本序列的形式传入。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate the effectiveness of Interaction-as-a-Judge for judging human preferences using ArenaPreferences (Figure 3 ). The code-only judge receives only the code as input, making it functionally identical to either LLM-as-a-Judge ( Zheng et al., 2023 ) or a standard code reward model. The code and screenshot judge receives the code and a full page screenshot of the landing page. This same screenshot is also given as input to Interaction-as-a-Judge approaches. We also vary the amount of code received between the full code capped at 32 32 k tokens and just the core App.tsx file to study the effects of code on Interaction-as-a-Judge. Additional information such as category breakdowns can be found in Appendix B .

paragraphs.en: To train our reward model, we fine-tune Qwen-3.5-9B ( Qwen Team, 2026 ) as our base model and train on a private dataset of 20,160 20,160 human preference pairs. This dataset is structurally identical to ArenaPreferences, but is temporally disjoint consisting of data prior to ArenaPreferences, mirroring how data collection occurs in real settings. This means that the reward model is evaluated on newer, more advanced outputs not seen in the training data. For the visual component of the interaction trace, we input it directly as video and freeze the video encoder weights during training.
paragraphs.zh: 为了训练我们的奖励模型，我们将 Qwen-3.5-9B（Qwen Team，2026）作为基础模型进行微调，并在一个包含 20,160 个人类偏好对的私有数据集上进行训练。 该数据集在结构上与 ArenaPreferences 完全相同，但在时间上相互独立，仅包含 ArenaPreferences 之前的数据，这反映了真实场景中的数据收集方式。 这意味着奖励模型是在训练数据中未出现过的、更新且更先进的输出结果上进行评估的。 对于交互轨迹中的视觉部分，我们直接将其作为视频输入，并在训练过程中冻结视频编码器的权重。

paragraphs.en: Interaction-as-a-Judge increases alignment with human preferences. We find that for both a trained reward model and an LLM Judge, adding interaction improves judge alignment with human preferences (Figure 3 ). Adding visual information through a screenshot improves performance over code and adding interaction improves performance further. We see the largest gap in Gemini 3 Flash as a judge where accuracy improves from 65.6 % → 69.1 % 65.6\%\rightarrow 69.1\% between code only and iterative Interaction-as-a-Judge. GPT 5.6 Luna as a judge is the sole exception where we do not see any statistical differences between any approach. We speculate that for pairwise preferences, GPT 5.6 Luna is both optimized for code and also unable to properly utilize visual information given its strong code-only performance and degradation when adding even a single screenshot. Finally, our trained reward model ( 70.8 % 70.8\% ) is able to outperform an off-the-shelf LLM judge ( 69.1 % 69.1\% ).
paragraphs.zh: “交互式法官”方法能增强与人类偏好的对齐程度。 我们发现，无论是训练好的奖励模型还是大型语言模型（LLM）法官，加入交互都能提升其与人类偏好的对齐程度（图3）。 通过截图添加视觉信息可提升性能，而加入交互则能进一步改善性能。 在 Gemini 3 Flash 作为法官时，我们观察到最大的差距：仅使用代码与迭代“交互式法官”方法之间的准确率从 65.6% 提升至 69.1%（65.6\%\rightarrow 69.1\%）。 GPT 5.6 Luna 作为法官是唯一例外，在所有方法之间均未观察到任何统计学上的差异。 我们推测，对于成对偏好判断，GPT 5.6 Luna 既针对代码进行了优化，又因其在仅使用代码时表现优异、而添加哪怕一张截图就会导致性能下降，因此无法有效利用视觉信息。 最后，我们训练好的奖励模型（70.8%（70.8\%））能够超越现成的 LLM 法官（69.1%（69.1\%））。

paragraphs.en: Interaction alone is sufficient information for training a reward model. We find that training a reward model on the interaction traces alone (without code) provides comparable performance to a code reward model. Iterative computer-use without code performs only slightly worse than a code reward model trained on the entire code context ( 69.0 % ​ vs ​ 69.7 % 69.0\%\ \text{vs}\ 69.7\% ), and performs comparably to Interaction-as-a-Judge with code when using Gemini 3 Flash as a judge. This opens doors to training reward models on data where the application is accessible, but code is inaccessible. In general, Interaction-as-a-Judge judgements remain robust as code context decreases, seeing small decreases between seeing the full source code versus only the core App.tsx file. However, both one-shot and heuristic computer-use degrade more compared to iterative computer-use when no code is available.
paragraphs.zh: 仅凭交互信息就足以训练奖励模型。 我们发现，仅使用交互轨迹（不含代码）训练奖励模型，其性能可与基于代码的奖励模型相媲美。 无需代码的迭代式计算机操作表现仅略低于在完整代码上下文中训练的代码奖励模型（69.0% vs 69.7%），并且在将 Gemini 3 Flash 用作评判者时，其表现与使用代码的“交互即评判”方法相当。 这为在应用程序可访问但代码不可获取的数据上训练奖励模型提供了可能性。 总体而言，“交互即评判”的判断结果在代码上下文减少时仍保持稳健，即使仅看到核心的 App.tsx 文件，其性能与看到完整源代码相比也仅有轻微下降。 然而，在没有代码可用的情况下，一次性使用和启发式计算机操作的性能相较于迭代式计算机操作的下降更为显著。

paragraphs.en: Interaction quality affects alignment with human preferences. We observe that iterative computer-use consistently performs the best across all experiments. Due to its ability to respond to new state changes in the environment, iterative computer-use generates the highest-quality traces among the three approaches. Additionally, we find that higher-quality interaction at inference can compensate for lower-quality traces at training time. We take our reward model trained on heuristic computer-use and run inference using iterative computer-use instead. We find that performance increases across almost every single category (Appendix F , Figure 12 ). The inverse is not true—a reward model trained on iterative computer-use degrades when using heuristic computer-use traces at inference time.

paragraphs.en: We evaluate Interaction-as-a-Judge on its ability to both verify and discover requirements using our ArenaCorrectness dataset (Figure 4 ). For requirement verification, we give the agent the code, the game as an interactable application, and the list of requirements which can be either all broken or all working. The agent is asked to label each requirement as working, broken, or unverifiable. paragraphs.en: We study the potential of Interaction-as-a-Judge at training time to improve downstream performance in generating interactive applications. Specifically, we explore using an interaction-only reward model as the reward signal for post-training via reinforcement learning (Figure 6 ). We start our training from Qwen-3.5-9B and use DAPO ( Yu et al., 2025 ) as our learning algorithm. We use the same interaction only reward model we trained in Section 4.1 and compare against a code only reward model. We use heuristic computer-use to reduce costs and training time. We train on a set of 14 14 k internal prompts that are not used for reward model training which cover all categories except for games as heuristic computer-use has difficulty playing games. We sample 600 examples uniformly from the six categories in ArenaPreferences as our test set. Since our reward model training data is cleaned to remove any failures, failures are out of distribution for both models. To account for this, we add penalties for any website that fails to build or render at all. Detailed hyperparameters can be found in Appendix G .

paragraphs.en: Overall, we observe that each model scores higher on their respective reward models, but interaction improves neutral objectives by reducing code generated and increasing successful builds. Code only reward models are known to have length bias ( Wang et al., 2026 ) —we observe that training on the interaction reward model generates 35.7 % 35.7\% less code than the code reward model. On our test set, Interaction-as-a-Judge also increases the build success rate from 81.3 % 81.3\% to 88.5 % 88.5\% compared to a code only reward model, reducing the build failure rate by 7.2 7.2 percentage points ( 18.7 % → 11.5 % 18.7\%\to 11.5\% ). We use an internal auto-rubrics based judge based on Kao et al. (2026) calibrated to Arena’s data and leaderboard to compare each trained model against Qwen-3.5-9B. Among websites that build and render successfully, the model trained using Interaction-as-a-Judge achieves a win-rate gain of 6.72 6.72 pp over the base model (Figure 6 ). Based on our internal calibrations, this is equivalent to over a 50 point increase on Arena’s leaderboard, which would be a statistically significant improvement to the model in Arena’s leaderboard. This evaluation measures quality conditioned on successful generations and therefore understates the benefit of using Interaction-as-a-Judge as a reward signal. The ability to train a model via reinforcement learning with an interaction only reward model opens the door to data collection opportunities where application access is available, but code access is not.
paragraphs.zh: 总体而言，我们观察到每个模型在其各自的奖励模型上得分更高，但交互方式通过减少生成的代码量并提高构建成功率，从而改进了中性目标。已知仅基于代码的奖励模型存在长度偏差（Wang 等人，2026）——我们观察到，在交互奖励模型上进行训练所生成的代码比仅基于代码的奖励模型少 35.7 %（35.7\%）。在我们的测试集上，与仅基于代码的奖励模型相比，“交互即裁判”方法还将构建成功率从 81.3 %（81.3\%）提升至 88.5 %（88.5\%），使构建失败率降低了 7.2 个百分点（18.7 % → 11.5 %，即 18.7\%\to 11.5\%）。我们使用一种基于 Kao 等人（2026）研究的内部自动评分规则裁判系统，该系统已根据 Arena 的数据和排行榜进行了校准，用以将每个训练好的模型与 Qwen-3.5-9B 进行比较。在能够成功构建和渲染的网站中，使用“交互即裁判”方法训练的模型相比基础模型实现了 6.72 个百分点（6.72 pp）的胜率提升（图 6）。根据我们的内部校准结果，这一提升相当于在 Arena 排行榜上超过 50 分的进步，这将在统计上显著改善该模型在 Arena 排行榜上的表现。本次评估是在生成成功的前提下衡量质量的，因此低估了将“交互即裁判”用作奖励信号所带来的益处。通过仅基于交互的奖励模型进行强化学习来训练模型的能力，为那些可以访问应用程序但无法访问代码的数据收集场景开辟了新的可能性。

paragraphs.en: The two most related families of work are other LLM-based judging strategies and existing instances where CUAs have been used for evaluation or generation. Unlike prior work, our work differs from the latter in that interaction is the central focus of our study, rather than one component of a larger pipeline. Specifically, we conduct the first systematic study spanning (i) the effects of varying interaction strategies and model capabilities on evaluation performance, (ii) measuring Interaction-as-a-Judge’s alignment with human preferences and correctness, and (iii) its use for both inference-time scaling and post-training. Below, we outline the connections more specifically.
paragraphs.zh: 最相关的两个研究领域是其他基于大型语言模型（LLM）的评估策略，以及现有将计算智能体（CUA）用于评估或生成的实例。 与以往的研究不同，我们的工作与后者存在差异：互动是我们研究的焦点，而非更大流程中的一个组成部分。 具体而言，我们开展了首个系统性研究，涵盖以下三个方面：(i) 不同互动策略和模型能力对评估表现的影响；(ii) 衡量“互动即判官”方法与人类偏好及正确性的一致性；以及 (iii) 其在推理阶段扩展和后训练阶段的应用。 下面，我们将更具体地阐述这些关联。

sents.en: Unlike prior work, our work differs from the latter in that interaction is the central focus of our study, rather than one component of a larger pipeline.
sents.zh: 与以往的研究不同，我们的工作与后者存在差异：互动是我们研究的焦点，而非更大流程中的一个组成部分。

sents.en: Specifically, we conduct the first systematic study spanning (i) the effects of varying interaction strategies and model capabilities on evaluation performance, (ii) measuring Interaction-as-a-Judge’s alignment with human preferences and correctness, and (iii) its use for both inference-time scaling and post-training.
sents.zh: 具体而言，我们开展了首个系统性研究，涵盖以下三个方面：(i) 不同互动策略和模型能力对评估表现的影响；(ii) 衡量“互动即判官”方法与人类偏好及正确性的一致性；以及 (iii) 其在推理阶段扩展和后训练阶段的应用。

sents.en: Below, we outline the connections more specifically.
sents.zh: 下面，我们将更具体地阐述这些关联。

paragraphs.en: LLM-as-a-Judge uses language models to approximate human judgments of generated outputs ( Zheng et al., 2023 ) . For software development, the evidence needed to judge requirement satisfaction can be distributed across a project and its development history. Agent-as-a-Judge ( Zhuge et al., 2024 ) addresses this by gathering and inspecting project files and development trajectories before judging. Interactive applications introduce a further source of evidence: the behavior observed when a user operates the software. Computer-use agents provide a means to collect this evidence by interacting with desktop and web interfaces ( Xie et al., 2024 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ; Koh et al., 2024 ) . Interaction-as-a-Judge extends these judging paradigms to this new source of evidence: rather than inspecting only static artifacts, the judge conditions on traces produced by a computer-use agent operating the application.
paragraphs.zh: LLM-as-a-Judge 利用语言模型来近似模拟人类对生成结果的判断（Zheng 等人，2023）。 在软件开发中，判断需求是否得到满足所需的证据可能分散在整个项目及其开发历史中。 Agent-as-a-Judge（Zhuge 等人，2024）通过在判断前收集并检查项目文件和开发轨迹来解决这一问题。 交互式应用引入了另一类证据：用户操作软件时观察到的行为。 计算机使用智能体通过与桌面和网页界面进行交互，为收集这类证据提供了手段（Xie 等人，2024；Zhou 等人，2024；Koh 等人，2024）。 Interaction-as-a-Judge 将这些判断范式扩展到了这一新的证据来源：判断者不再仅检查静态产物，而是以计算机使用智能体操作应用时产生的轨迹作为条件进行判断。

paragraphs.en: Recent works have attempted to use computer-use as part of their evaluation pipeline. ArtifactsBench ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) and GameCraft-Bench ( Luo et al., 2026 ) ground judgments in heuristically generated screenshots and replayed gameplay, respectively. AppEvalPilot ( Bian et al., 2025 ) generates and executes test cases using a computer-use agent and validates its judgments against human assessments of functional requirements. In these works, interaction is used as a method of evaluation rather than the focus of study, and it remains unclear how computer-use model capabilities and methods of interaction affect evaluation performance. WebDevJudge ( Li et al., 2025 ) , which benchmarks LLM and multimodal judges for web development, illustrates the importance of understanding these capabilities as it finds that its standalone GUI-agent workflow actually underperforms its strongest static judges due to errors arising during planning and execution.
paragraphs.zh: 近期的研究尝试将计算机使用作为其评估流程的一部分。 ArtifactsBench（Zhang 等人，2025）和 GameCraft-Bench（Luo 等人，2026）分别基于启发式生成的屏幕截图和重播的游戏过程来建立判断基准。 AppEvalPilot（Bian 等人，2025）通过一个计算机使用智能体生成并执行测试用例，并将其判断结果与人类对功能需求的评估进行验证。 在这些研究中，交互被用作一种评估方法，而非研究的核心；目前尚不清楚计算机使用模型的能力及交互方式如何影响评估表现。 WebDevJudge（Li 等人，2025）对大型语言模型和多模态法官在网页开发领域的表现进行基准测试，它表明理解这些能力至关重要：研究发现，其独立的 GUI 智能体工作流程由于规划和执行过程中出现的错误，实际表现反而弱于其最强的静态法官。

paragraphs.en: Interaction evidence can also guide the generation process that produces an application. WebGen-Agent ( Lu et al., 2025 ) incorporates screenshot feedback and iterative computer-use testing into website refinement. For reinforcement learning, it sums screenshot-based appearance scores and GUI-testing scores, and introduces Step-GRPO to assign advantages separately to each refinement step. Wang et al. (2026) use one-shot computer-use: a model plans the full action sequence upfront, and a rubric-based judge scores the recorded execution to provide training rewards, reducing code-length exploitation compared to static judges. Both approaches obtain their reward signals from model-generated assessments of appearance or functionality. We provide an alternative and potentially simpler solution by training a reward model on human preferences ( Christiano et al., 2017 ; Ouyang et al., 2022 ) using interaction traces and then using its predictions as outcome rewards in DAPO.
paragraphs.zh: 交互证据也可以指导生成应用程序的过程。WebGen-Agent（Lu 等人，2025）将屏幕截图反馈和迭代计算机使用测试整合到了网站优化过程中。对于强化学习，该方法将基于屏幕截图的外观得分与 GUI 测试得分相加，并引入 Step-GRPO 为每一步优化单独分配优势值。Wang 等人（2026）采用了一次性计算机使用策略：模型预先规划完整的动作序列，然后由基于评分标准的评判器对记录下来的执行过程进行评分，从而提供训练奖励；与静态评判器相比，这种方法减少了因代码长度过长而导致的过度利用问题。这两种方法都是从模型对外观或功能性的评估中获得奖励信号的。我们提出了一种替代方案，该方案可能更为简单：通过交互痕迹，在人类偏好数据上训练一个奖励模型（Christiano 等人，2017；Ouyang 等人，2022），然后将该模型的预测结果作为 DAPO 中的结果奖励。

paragraphs.en: While we study some common approaches to computer-use, we believe that better computer-use models and methods could further improve evaluation and generation, especially considering our observation that better computer-use traces lead to better performance. Currently, one of the biggest bottlenecks to computer-use remains cost. For example, we were mostly limited to experiments with GPT 5.6 Luna as our computer use agent due to pricing. More capable and affordable computer-use agents will likely improve Interaction-as-a-Judge capabilities and are worth studying as well. For training, there is the possibility of using the same model for both generation and computer-use and improving them both simultaneously as better applications and better traces both improve reward modeling scores. We leave this as potential future work.

paragraphs.en: We study Interaction-as-a-Judge, an evaluation paradigm that uses computer-use traces to improve evaluation and downstream generation. We study the use of Interaction-as-a-Judge for both human preferences and correctness verification, releasing two datasets—ArenaPreferences and ArenaCorrectness—to facilitate such studies. We demonstrate how Interaction-as-a-Judge improves alignment with human preferences for both reward model training and LLM judges and improves a model’s ability to label requirements as working or broken. We show how Interaction-as-a-Judge can be used for inference-time scaling through an iterative self-feedback loop. Lastly, we illustrate how you can use a reward model trained on only interaction traces, with no code, as the reward signal for standard reinforcement learning training.
paragraphs.zh: 我们研究了“交互即评判”（Interaction-as-a-Judge）这一评估范式，它利用计算机使用痕迹来改进评估和下游生成任务。 我们探讨了“交互即评判”在人类偏好判断和正确性验证中的应用，并发布了两个数据集——ArenaPreferences 和 ArenaCorrectness——以支持相关研究。 我们展示了“交互即评判”如何提升奖励模型训练和大型语言模型（LLM）评判器对人类偏好的对齐能力，并增强模型将需求标记为“可用”或“故障”的能力。 我们说明了如何通过迭代自反馈循环，在推理阶段利用“交互即评判”实现模型扩展。 最后，我们展示了如何仅使用基于交互痕迹训练的奖励模型（无需任何代码）作为标准强化学习训练中的奖励信号。

paragraphs.en: For preference prediction, we render each candidate in a separate Chromium browser context using Playwright. Applications run inside an iframe with a 1280 × 800 1280\times 800 viewport and device scale factor one. Mouse coordinates are measured in pixels relative to the top-left corner of the application iframe. Each tool response contains a screenshot of the application, the viewport dimensions, cursor position, held keys, and execution status. The interactive agent receives the original user request and these observations. The one-shot agent additionally receives application source code when constructing its action sequence. For pairwise preferences, the agents explore each candidate independently and then the preference judge subsequently compares the resulting evidence for both candidates. For correctness verification, the same agent explores and judges the candidate in one continuous workflow.

paragraphs.en: The main preference experiments use a budget of 30 interaction steps per candidate. A step is one tool invocation, which can itself contain several low-level input events: for example, a click includes a mouse press and release, while press_keys executes a sequence of key presses. The computer-use agent is allowed to exit early if it determines that its goal is complete.

paragraphs.en: For games, a JavaScript timing shim wraps animation frames, timers, and application clocks. The game is paused between actions, and ordinary actions advance its clock by 500 ms. Key holds and waits advance the requested duration, capped by the per-step budget. This separates model inference latency from simulated game time. The timing shim advances in small increments so that animation callbacks can execute between inputs. Other web applications run in real time and are allowed to settle after an action.
paragraphs.zh: 在游戏场景中，一个 JavaScript 计时辅助层会封装动画帧、计时器和应用时钟。 游戏在两次操作之间处于暂停状态，普通操作会使游戏时钟推进 500 毫秒。 按键长按和等待操作会按请求的时长推进时间，但受限于每步的时间预算。 这样就能将模型推理延迟与模拟的游戏时间区分开来。 该计时辅助层以微小增量推进时间，以便在输入之间能够执行动画回调函数。 其他网页应用则以实时运行，并允许在操作结束后完成处理。

paragraphs.en: For non-gaming applications, the heuristic enumerates visible, enabled controls in the current viewport: links, buttons, input fields, text areas, selects, summaries, elements with relevant accessibility roles, click handlers, or a non-negative tab index. It excludes hidden and off-screen controls, deduplicates controls by their center coordinates, and retains at most 200 candidates. Candidate controls are sampled uniformly. A text field is clicked before entering a phrase drawn from a fixed small vocabulary, and a PageDown action is sampled with probability 0.12 0.12 to reveal additional content. If no candidates are found, the policy falls back to pixel and keyboard actions.
paragraphs.zh: 对于非游戏类应用，启发式方法会枚举当前视口中可见且已启用的控件：链接、按钮、输入框、文本区域、选择框、摘要、具有相关无障碍角色的元素、点击处理程序或非负的 tab 索引。 它会排除隐藏和位于屏幕外的控件，根据控件的中心坐标去除重复项，并最多保留 200 个候选项。 候选控件以均匀方式采样。 在输入短语之前，会先点击一个文本框；该短语来自一个固定的小型词汇表，并以 0.12 的概率采样 PageDown 操作以显示更多内容。 如果未找到任何候选项，策略将回退到像素和键盘操作。

paragraphs.en: Games differ from other categories in two ways. First, games often require real-time input, so we construct a web harness that freezes games between interactions and plays actions out for up to 500 milliseconds (i.e., 2 actions per second). Second, since games typically do not have clear interaction candidates (e.g., buttons), heuristic computer-use actions are drawn uniformly from a 12-element action space consisting of four click actions, three key-sequence actions, two key-hold actions, and one each of mouse movement, drag, and double click. Coordinates are sampled uniformly within the viewport. Keyboard actions are sampled from the four arrow keys, Space, Enter, and w , a , s , and d .
paragraphs.zh: 游戏与其他类别在两个方面有所不同。 首先，游戏通常需要实时输入，因此我们构建了一个网络框架，在交互之间冻结游戏，并以最多 500 毫秒（即每秒 2 个动作）的速度执行动作。 其次，由于游戏通常没有明确的交互选项（例如按钮），启发式计算机操作动作会从包含 12 个元素的动作空间中均匀抽取，该空间由四个点击动作、三个按键序列动作、两个按键长按动作，以及各一个鼠标移动、拖动和双击动作组成。 坐标在视口内均匀采样。 键盘动作从四个方向键、空格键、回车键以及 w、a、s 和 d 键中采样。

paragraphs.en: Figures 7 and 8 expand the LLM-judge comparison. Figures 9 and 10 give the corresponding reward-model results under the two code representations. All bars measure agreement with the original human preferences. The overall panels weight categories by their number of battles rather than assigning each category equal weight. Bold values indicate positive paired gains over code+screenshot with p < 0.05 p<0.05 , calculated using a two-sided paired test. Across 28 category comparisons, iterative interaction significantly outperformed code+screenshot in 14, significantly underperformed in one, and showed no statistically significant difference in 13. Across the four approaches, simulations and games show the largest average accuracy gains from iterative interaction over code+screenshot (+2.81 and +1.74 percentage points, respectively). paragraphs.en: The full-code comparison allows 100,000 source characters before applying the 32,768-token sequence limit. Its source pipeline removes lockfiles, selects files under the character budget, and orders the selected files from smaller to larger with the main application file placed last. paragraphs.en: To distinguish visual observations from their accompanying text, we train 9B models with four input representations: code alone; code with actions and intermediate reasoning but no images; code with video frames but no trace text; and code with both video and trace text. paragraphs.en: As mentioned in the main paper, website failures are out of distribution for our training and test sets. As a result, we introduce some penalties for various types of build failures. The common failure rewards are − 5 -5 for no submitted build, − 4.5 -4.5 for a build failure, − 4 -4 for an environment crash, and − 3.5 -3.5 for a render failure. Successful applications receive the corresponding scalar reward-model score, followed by the configured overlength penalty from DAPO. The code-only arm retains the same build and render checks, despite not presenting visual input to its learned judge. Non-gaming browser interaction uses the DOM-aware heuristic described in Appendix A .
paragraphs.zh: 正如主论文中提到的，网站故障在我们的训练集和测试集中属于分布外事件。 因此，我们对各类构建失败引入了相应的惩罚机制。 常见的失败奖励为：未提交构建时减 5（-5），构建失败时减 4.5（-4.5），环境崩溃时减 4（-4），渲染失败时减 3.5（-3.5）。 成功的应用程序将获得对应的标量奖励模型分数，随后应用来自 DAPO 的已配置过长惩罚。 仅含代码的分支仍保留相同的构建和渲染检查，尽管它不会向已学习的评判器提供视觉输入。 非游戏类的浏览器交互使用附录 A 中描述的 DOM 感知启发式方法。
